cover.prose:
The source image — an isometric block city over a strategy-breeding harness — works because of three quiet decisions, and only one of them is the city: it maps roles in a mechanism rather than files; it spends its one visual scalar (height) on a true quantity; and it keeps a CONDITION field that says what is currently wrong. This set keeps those three decisions and lets everything else change with altitude.

The result is an argument about form: a loop where there is a genuine cycle (sheet 1), panels where packages are too small to be cities (sheet 2), the full city where the measurement thesis is actually true (sheet 3), a massed spine where the family shares one core but the limbs never touch (sheet 4), a chart where edges would be fiction (sheet 5), and mostly prose where only a definition survives (sheet 6). Fitness peaks in the middle altitudes and collapses at both ends.

Above the sixth altitude the set stops arguing about form and starts measuring. Sheets 7–10 are a survey quartet, each counting the same subject at a different boundary: what the repository holds (the monorepo by mass), what npm delivers (the sample app's node_modules, 269× the app it serves), what the browser downloads (the docs deploy on the wire, where the prerendered prose tops the skyline and the lettering alone outweighs every routed app the site demonstrates), and who occupies the bytes after tree-shaking (the machine the router wraps is 21.9% of the bundle; the router itself, 4.7%). Sheet 11 cuts the same wire the other way, pricing 7 package quarters and 22 doors one at a time. Sheet 12 leaves the wire and draws the monorepo as its own CI reads it, the pull-request task graph punched onto a register plate. Sheet 13 ages the city by commit date. Interactive lanes (1i, 2B, 12i and the three.js city) walk the plates they sit beside. The appendix files plates whose subject is the atlas rather than the codebase: the sprite study behind the building sprites (appendix A1), and the survey office that turns the instrument on itself (appendix A2) — the census pipeline behind almost every number here, drawn as archive → probe stations → filed plates → drawings, introspected from the generator at build time, and walked live in its lane A2i.

cover.thesis: Riffs on an isometric codebase-visualization form seen in the wild; the notes on each sheet argue where that form fits and where it lies.
cover.notes: Static HTML pages, written by node generator/build.mjs . from this directory. The SVG sheets need nothing; the interactive plates (1i, 2B, 12i, 7·3D and appendix A2i) load cytoscape 3.31.0 and three.js 0.169.0 from cdnjs, which generator/stage-site.mjs vendors for hosting. app/ is the same set as a prerendered lit-ui-router app; build.mjs emits its fragments and manifest. On the published site the app owns the root (/, /sheet/7, /city) and this flat set is staged beside it under /set/ as the version to compare against; the two link to each other (the app's rail and crumbs, the gallery's cover). Light theme is graphite-on-vellum; dark is cyanotype. Since 2026-09-06 every label on the plates draws in the data face (DIN 2014, Barlow Semi Condensed off the kit) rather than the system monospace; mono is reserved for code. Generated 2026-08-16 by Fable (Claude, AI). Every plate in data/ — versions, dates and all — was re-counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e in one pass, plate 7A's test light included: generator/census-shadow.mjs re-meters it at the same ref. The cover's general survey — every tracked file on the scc 4.0.0 Code basis, origin/main @ 6d41d21e — is imported from data/census-files.json, the master snapshot generator/census-scc.mjs writes; generator/census-overview.mjs prints the same rollup on the terminal.

sheets.title: THE RENDER LOOP
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 1 — lit-ui-router 1.16.0 · the client circuit drawn as one isometric scene: every leg of the loop is a road on the grid, the document a browser window whose DOM rises in plates, and the six package entries a door strip along the footer · version read from census-files.json
sheets.caption: The loop sits on the ground: every leg is a road that turns along the iso axes and stops short of the wall it points at. The city breaks its metaphor once, on purpose — the document is not a building but a browser window whose DOM rises in plates. The core matches, the hall runs its hook bays, Lit commits onto a layer, and a click on the topmost plate flies back to location.
sheets.verdict: strong fit — the render cycle is a genuine circuit

sheets.title: THE RENDER LOOP, WALKED
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 1 — sheet 1's circuit, stepped · one navigation walked leg by leg · 10 STATIONS · 12 LEGS · 12 STEPS · surveyed at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (commit 2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: The circuit, stood up and stepped. 10 stations and 12 legs, then one click — a click on <a uiSref> from /people to /people/32 — walked in 12 steps under the pointer, every step standing on the 30 source lines the plate cites verbatim.

sheets.title: THE BRICK ASSEMBLY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2 — one baseplate, six bricks, 53 authored files · an exploded LEGO assembly with every coupling named to the API call that makes it, brick and stud faces drawn opaque so nothing reads through a mass in front of it · REV F 2026-10-04: the finished model joins the exploded view — the same parts seated in three steps at the drawing’s own corner, then the whole from two more corners, in a landscape of two levels — browser ground under the client plate, a server shelf under the headless plate — so the bridge spans the no-DOM line · source counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: Every companion drawn here enters through a published stud — on @uirouter/core, or on a brick that publishes one of its own. Drawn exploded, the sheet answers the only question that matters about a plugin architecture: pull any brick off and what breaks? Only what stands on it — three bricks seat on lit-ui-router, one of them on the server too — and the plate’s studs stay where they are.
sheets.verdict: exploded, then seated: every coupling is a published stud, on core or on the brick below — and the server takes none of core’s

sheets.title: THE COUPLING PLAN
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2 — ALTERNATE PLATE: the six companions sheet 2 seats, laid out for reading — core central as a socket wall, companions at its right, the server below the no-DOM line — with every coupling drawn disengaged and lettered to its API call · rows read census-bricks.json @ 6d41d21e
sheets.caption: The brick assembly, uncoupled and brought down to one elevation: core as a socket wall, companions as shallow blocks drawn just short of seated, and each of the six connection points on the wall — five published studs and one keyed red seat — large enough to letter its API call on the joint itself. Three more joints are companion-to-companion, and one of those spans both halves of the plate.

sheets.title: THE COUPLING BENCH
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2 — INTERACTIVE PLATE: sheet 2A’s joints made live · 9 nodes in four columns, every tie a straight run · each of the 14 drawn edges is a published contract, with its declared range under the pointer
sheets.caption: The same assembly as sheets 2 and 2A, reduced to what a consumer's installer actually reads: 9 buildings and 14 contracts. Hover an edge for the range it declares and the section it lives in; hover a building for its version, what it declares, and what declares it.
sheets.verdict: 2A’s joints made live — every one of the 14 drawn edges is a published contract with its declared range under the pointer: 20 peers to 3 dependencies across the 7 packages, and no dependency is a router

sheets.title: THE INSTRUMENT YARD
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3 — 7 publishable packages · 24 tools · 89 turbo task names · one packer, many readers · every mass counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03) from www/atlas.lit-ui-router.dev/data/census-yard.json on scc Code lines — 253 authored files and 19,006 sloc across 17 massed structures, with the task-manager inset reading the same two plates sheet 3A draws
sheets.caption: The monorepo drawn as what it functionally is: a short conveyor that turns source into one tarball, inside a yard of instruments built to measure that tarball. Every structure carries its measured mass — footprint ∝ √sloc, height ∝ authored files — and gate severity is colour rather than height, because the two do not correlate: the blocks that stop the line are among the smallest on the sheet.
sheets.verdict: the yard re-massed from sloc × files — gate severity in colour: the smallest blocks stop the line; the task-manager inset reads the same plates as 3A, so the two cannot disagree

sheets.title: THE HANDOFF WORKS
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3 · ALTERNATE PLATE — the sheet-3 task-manager inset at full size: 8 of 13 workflows · 54 mise tasks in 4 homes · turbo ci 863 nodes, 234 real · 4 seam types · 3 service doors · every frame sized to the widest DIN line it holds, so the spine is computed rather than hand-set · every count imported from www/atlas.lit-ui-router.dev/data/census-handoff.json + census-plate.json · counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: The two task managers drawn as the two machines they are — mise the node-free umbrella, turbo the cached fan-out — with the seams as the featured parts: every crossing is a bolted gasket labeled with what crosses it and what the boundary buys. The star fitting is the cache gasket on the return duct: turbo caches mise, because the six re-entrant lint lanes hash the mise task files and mise.lock, so a tool-pin bump invalidates exactly its own lane.
sheets.verdict: turbo caches mise — and the loop is a DAG in a loop costume: the 7 tasks that shell turbo and the 8 turbo re-enters never touch; every count imported, turbo at 126 definitions in 22 files

sheets.title: THE WATCHED CITY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3 · ALTERNATE PLATE B — the PR ci graph as a city: 234 real tasks in 29 massed structures · footprint = watched files (13,064 task-file hashes) · height = command sloc (2,921) · 629 phantom plots · every number imported from www/atlas.lit-ui-router.dev/data/census-mass3b.json, surveyed at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: The pull-request graph that plate 3A traced as plumbing, surveyed here as ground: every real task massed by what it watches (footprint) and what it actually executes (height). The survey’s verdict is flatness — 184 of 234 blocks are a single script line riding an external binary — which makes the exceptions legible at a glance: a 293-line test tower on a 38-file lot, and a 363-file plain patrolled by 20 lines of command.
sheets.verdict: footprint = watched files, height = command sloc — 184 of 234 tasks are one-line pads; the tallest is the 401-sloc //#lint:elements spire

sheets.title: THE FAMILY SPINE
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 4 — one core, four living adapters, four dormant instruments, massed by authored source and gated on the core range each admits · versions npm registry read 2026-10-03, mass counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: Not a loop and not a city: a spine. Every limb shares @uirouter/core and no limb talks to another, so the honest drawing is radial. Each block is massed from its own authored source and each stem crosses a gate naming the core range that limb admits — and the gates do not agree.
sheets.verdict: every limb re-massed from sloc × files — one red gate: @uirouter/react pins core as a dependency

sheets.title: THE DESIGN SPACE
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 5 — ten routers placed by where matching happens and who owns navigation, shape marking the source of truth · positions are editorial, argued in the notes
sheets.caption: No mechanism connects these projects, so any drawn edge would be fiction. What is real is position: where matching happens, who owns navigation, and — the one square — whether the URL or a state tree is the source of truth.
sheets.verdict: no shared mechanism — position, not edges

sheets.title: THE ROUTING STRATA
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 6 — routing in general · the altitude where prose outranks pictures
sheets.caption: At the widest altitude the only shared structure is a definition, so the drawing shrinks to a core sample and the writing does the work: five strata, one invariant triple.
sheets.verdict: prose outranks pictures; one small column earns its place

sheets.title: THE MEASURED CITY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3½ — the same city as sheet 3, surveyed by mass · 39 members in 4 districts, footprint ∝ √sloc, height ∝ authored files, spec mass drawn as an annex, gate severity in colour · counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: Sheet 3 drew the monorepo as a process; this sheet counts who lives in it. Footprint ∝ √sloc, height ∝ authored files, tests drawn as annexes rather than deleted — and over that census the two things a census alone cannot say: which district each member belongs to, and which roads run between them. Every road is a workspace dependency or a turbo task edge, never an impression.
sheets.verdict: the census with districts and roads — tests as annexes, every edge cited: the 14-line harness stops every PR, and all 39 members are measured on the scc ruler

sheets.title: THE SHADOW SURVEY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3½ — ALTERNATE PLATE TO SHEET 7: the measured city under its own test light · same city as sheet 7, 39 members · reach = the source each suite loads, brightness = line coverage of what it loads · metered at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: This plate asks which members of sheet 7’s city ever stand in test light. Every member’s own suite runs under a coverage meter, and its light is drawn to two rules: reach, how much of the member’s source the suite loads; brightness, the line coverage of what it loads. The finding is a repo-wide habit visible from the air: the light is bright far more often than it is wide.
sheets.verdict: the shadow survey — the tests are the light: where a suite reaches it burns near-full — 25 members read under their own suites' meters at 6d41d21e, so the light and the census are one measurement

sheets.title: THE WORKING CITY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3½ — SYNTHESIS PLATE TO SHEET 7: the census city as a working plant · weathering (13) × test light (7A) × gates (7) × live build, one sprite per member · steam window 2026-07-05..2026-10-03 · counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: Sheet 7 counted the city, sheet 13 dated its stone, plate 7A metered its test light. This plate turns the same city on: every member becomes a Working Plant sprite in the Factorio sense — a machine whose state is broadcast, not implied. The alert channel is drawn and empty: no gate in the city is red at HEAD.
sheets.verdict: the synthesis plate — rust, steam, lamps and pipes on one city: 38 plants run and every pipe connects on 31 green build tasks, 25 carry metered lamps, and the alert register stands drawn and empty — no gate is red at HEAD

sheets.title: THE DELIVERED CITY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 1½ — what npm actually installs for one consumer · sample-app-lit-vanilla · 32 delivered packages, 173,596 lines of code and 41,079 d.ts lines on disk, footprint from files and height from lines — measured at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03), closure of apps/sample-app-lit-vanilla
sheets.caption: The production dependency closure of one sample app, surveyed on disk: every delivered package as a building — footprint from file count, height from lines — with the consumer’s own 646-line building standing in the city it summoned.
sheets.verdict: node_modules surveyed — 32 delivered packages, 269× the app that installs them

sheets.title: THE SHIPPED CITY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2¾ — what the browser downloads · lit-ui-router.dev, one deploy · 890 files in 12 districts, 4.7 MB on the wire, footprint from file count and height from gzipped bytes — measured at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03) · www/atlas.lit-ui-router.dev/generator/census-shipped.mjs
sheets.caption: The production docs deploy surveyed on the wire: 890 files, 4.7 MB gzipped, drawn as 12 districts — the tallest towers are prerendered prose and font files, the routed apps are 317 KB of accent buildings in their own city, and there is no ghost block: the deploy carries no unreachable files at all.
sheets.verdict: the wire survey — the deploy's tallest district is html pages at 1761 KB, and the lettering alone outweighs every routed app the site exists to demonstrate (848 KB against 317 KB)

sheets.title: THE BUNDLED CITY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2⅞ — inside the wire: what the bundler kept · one production bundle: 14 package groups in 17 chunks, 122,792 gz, footprint from source kept and height from wire share — apps/sample-app-lit-vanilla · counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: One shipped bundle opened up: every package that survived tree-shaking as a building — footprint from source kept, height from gzipped wire share — and the machine the router wraps, the chrome that demos it, and the app that uses it stand as three districts summing to 119.9 KB.
sheets.verdict: tree-shaking’s verdict — core is 21.9%, the router 4.7% — one lit

sheets.title: THE ENTRY QUARTERS
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2⅞ — the same wire, cut by published package · every exported entry priced alone · 22 doors in 7 package quarters, footprint from minified bytes and height from gzipped, dependencies external — counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03)
sheets.caption: The split view to sheet 10’s unified city: every exported entry of every publishable package bundled alone and priced — 7 package quarters, 22 doors, the codecov bundle-analysis series drawn as skylines.
sheets.verdict: the split view — 22 doors priced alone across 7 quarters; the cheapest is «./location» at 329 b, and the lint plugin's is the one door no browser opens

sheets.title: THE REGISTER PLATE
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3¼ — the monorepo as its CI reads it · every task node punched · surveyed at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (2026-10-03) · turbo 2.11.5
sheets.caption: The pull-request graph is a near-rectangle: 39 packages against 22 fanned task names, plus a ragged tail of 39 one-offs. 73% of the holes are unpunched — placeholder nodes that run nothing, minted so a ^self chain has somewhere to land an edge or an umbrella something to fan out from.
sheets.verdict: the punched inventory — 73% of the graph runs nothing, and the real→real edges that remain are a thin core inside a large node count

sheets.title: THE REGISTER, WALKED
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3¼ — sheet 12's plate, live under the pointer · the whole ci graph carried node by node · 863 NODES · 234 RUN A COMMAND · 2,985 EDGES · 109 JOIN TWO REAL TASKS · surveyed at origin/main @ 6d41d21e (commit 2026-10-03) · turbo 2.11.5
sheets.caption: The punchcard, stood up. Default view is the real subgraph alone — 234 tasks that run a command over 109 edges that join two of them. PHANTOM SHROUD floods in the other 629 nodes and 2,876 edges, and 72.9% of the graph stops being a statistic.
sheets.verdict: sheet 12's punchcard with a pointer in it — the whole ci graph carried node by node, real subgraph by default, and one checkbox that floods the 73% that runs nothing

sheets.title: THE WEATHERING MAP
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE t — the same city as sheet 7, surveyed in time · 442 files dated from the whole history · three construction seasons, 10 silent months · counted at origin/main @ 6d41d21e
sheets.caption: Every sheet so far has drawn the city as it stands; this one dates the stone. Same districts and footprints as sheet 7, but the fills now say when each file was first committed and the edges how often it is touched. The history is three construction campaigns separated by silent months, and the two encodings disagree on purpose: 91% of the city is summer-built and barely weathered, while the port’s original masonry carries the hottest edges on the map.
sheets.verdict: 91% of the city is summer stone — and the port’s original masonry, 26 files from 2025-07-21, carries the hottest edges

appendix.title: THE SPRITE STUDY
appendix.sub: APPENDIX · META — the research behind the building sprites, drawn in the set it argues about · three concepts on one demo member, five states each · and, at the foot, the reference strip itself: six fair-use thumbnails at reference size, credited — the set draws no images anywhere else
appendix.caption: Every other plate in this set measures the codebase. This one measures a decision: how a workspace member should look when a sheet draws it as a building. One demo member is drawn fifteen times, five states along a wreck-to-splendor gauge under three competing treatments, and each treatment is priced. The verdict stands in the set: sheet 7B is the working plant, and sheet 13 the weathering gauge.
appendix.verdict: meta — the research behind the building sprites, argued on one demo member in fifteen blocks: the working plant wins on cost and independence and shipped as sheet 7B, the vines are its second layer, and the ledger roof stays parked until a sheet wants per-file stories

appendix.title: THE SURVEY OFFICE

appendix.caption: The instrument drawn by its own instrument: 17 probe stations over three tiers write 17 filed plates, which 20 drawings read — and the one that matters most is read thirteen times over.
